item.title: Man arrested for trying to open Cathay Pacific plane door mid-flight
item.description: A 20-year-old male passenger on a Cathay Pacific flight from Boston to Hong Kong was arrested by police after allegedly attempting to open an aircraft door mid-flight on Thursday morning. The incident occurred around 15 minutes before the aircraft landed at Hong Kong International Airport at 4.45am on Thursday, local media outlet HK01 reported. According […]

item.title: Hong Kong activist ‘terrified’ as sexually explicit deepfake images sent to UK neighbours
item.description: A Hong Kong activist living in exile in the UK said Thursday she was “shocked and terrified” after discovering her neighbours received letters containing AI-generated sexually explicit images of her. item.title: US, Japan defence chiefs agree China harming regional peace
item.description: By Hiroshi Hiyama Beijing’s actions are “not conducive to regional peace”, Japan’s defence minister and US counterpart Pete Hegseth agreed during a call after Chinese aircraft locked radar on Japanese jets near Taiwan, Tokyo said Friday. item.title: Domestic worker injured in Tai Po fire returns to Philippines after hospital discharge
item.description: A Filipina domestic worker caught in the fatal Tai Po fire a day after arriving in the city has been discharged from hospital and will be returning home, according to an NGO. item.title: Judge David Lok to lead Tai Po fire review committee; probe due in 9 months
item.description: High Court Judge David Lok, who also heads the Hong Kong Electoral Affairs Commission, will chair the independent review committee investigating the deadly Tai Po fire. item.title: Hong Kong national security police arrest 9 men for alleged military-style ‘unlawful drills’
item.description: Hong Kong national security police have arrested nine men for allegedly engaging in “unlawful drills” involving military-style firearms and combat training. The nine suspects, aged 20 to 25, were arrested on Thursday night, police said on Friday. Authorities invoked the “illegal drilling” provision under the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, Hong Kong’s homegrown security law also […]

item.title: HKFP Monitor Dec 13, 2025: How Hong Kong mourned Tai Po fire victims; new ‘all patriots’ legislature
item.description: This week, we round up the different ways Hong Kong grieved for the victims of the deadly Tai Po fire, which has claimed at least 160 lives.
